small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_N tiles (e.g. 256, 512) to gemm_lse_kernel since N=1024 — fewer outer-loop iterations and better K-loop amortization; also try BLOCK_M=16/32 with BLOCK_N=512 to keep occupancy.
- Pre-transpose linear1.weight to a contiguous (K,N) buffer at init so gemm_sigmoid_kernel does pure row-major loads on B (currently using stride(1),stride(0) gives strided B loads); same for w2_h.
- Add autotune configs with num_stages=4-5 and BLOCK_K=64/128 for stage 1 (K=2048 is large, more pipelining helps); also try storing stage-1 output in fp16 with BLOCK_M=256 to reduce kernel launches.
large_guidance:
- Fuse stages: make a single persistent kernel where each program owns a row tile of M, computes the hidden vector h = sigmoid(x@W1+b1) for its rows keeping h in shared memory / registers, then streams W2 to compute logits and does online-LSE in one pass — eliminates the full hidden tensor write/read (16384×4096 fp16 ≈ 128MB of traffic).
- Alternatively, split-K stage 1 across SMs with atomic-free partial accumulation into a workspace, then a small epilogue kernel applies sigmoid+stage2; pick split factor to fully occupy all 128 SMs on the 4090.
- Consider tensor-core fp16 inputs for stage 1 too (cast x and W1 to fp16/bf16 once) — current stage 1 runs fp32xfp32 tl.dot which is ~half the TC throughput of fp16 accumulation on Ada.
